Suggested common name: Rainbow bitterling.

Origin: China. Available size: 8–10 cm.

Acheilognathus: ancient Greek, roughly meaning "without lips on the jaws". tonkinensis: after a geographical term ("Tonkin") for the northernmost part of Vietnam.
For our customers: the fish have code 800154 on our stocklist. Please note that we exclusively supply the wholesale trade.
This species originates from southern China, Vietnam and Laos.
Keeping these subtropical animals is without problems. It is not necessary to heat the tank as long as it is placed in a house; this makes the fish energy saving and environmental friendly.
Bitterlings feed on all types of commercial fishfood. Plants are usually ignored; if a bitterling starts nibbling on plants, the keeper should add more plant material to the fishfood.
Bitterlings are extremely peaceful to all tankmates.
The males shimmer in all colours of a rainbow, whereas the females are rather dull coloured and look like a typical "whitefish".
All species of bitterling are brood parasites: they place their eggs in living freshwater mussels, where the eggs hatch.

The bitterlings are a subfamily of the great and diverse carp family. So far only very few species have been introduced in the hobby, but there are about 70 species and subspecies classified in 4 genera. It is a pity that so few aquarists are interested in bitterlings, as all species are brilliantly coloured and very interesting due to their brood parasitism.

This very deep-bodied species becomes about 10 cm long. It is one of the most magnificent bitterlings of all, imported once more from China.

Text & photos: Frank Schäfer
